acceptance: The first page states what the Cloud project gives (Agents, teammates, history) before offering one action, Upload to Cloud, beside Not now; the confirmation that follows says the Cloud project is made from the folder's tracked files as a separate project and who will see it, and only Confirm starts the publication for the chosen organization. An unfinished publication is the progress standing still at its step with exactly Discard and Retry (or Push latest / reconcile as its actions say); Discard asks first, inline, with Cancel and Discard; an unfinished discard says so, offers only Discard and draws no send steps, says Discarding while it runs, and shows why it failed; a refused discard offers sending again and no Discard; a run in flight draws its step with Continue in background. A run keeps going when the dialog is put away, and the folder stays the open project.

Signed out, the publication waits passively for the account. It sends a named branch's committed tree and never snapshots the dirty checkout; a plain folder is first made into one committed branch; the coordinator's stages drive the progress while it runs; a retry keeps the exact Project and source branch after the checkout switches branches, and a missing source is replaced by the checked-out branch only when chosen; a typed failure is kept for an explicit retry; cleanup finishes for the exact operation; another checkout or account drops the shown result and error.

The Header states the publication beside the location and reopens the same view: a run in flight spins; a stopped run keeps its state until it is resolved; a saved unfinished publication is a warning after a restart too, and becomes the spinner the moment a retry runs; an unfinished discard is stated as a discard, never as a send to retry.

reason: TS's Header knows whether the dialog is watching the run: it leaves a watched run's ending to the dialog, shows a fresh unwatched failure before the paused task it leaves, and announces an unwatched success only briefly. The native Header states the publication the same way whether or not the dialog shows it, and a finished publication stays announced until the person clicks it or the checkout or account changes.

These lock the DOM of TS's pre-extraction initialization view (CloudLocalOnlyWorkspace) per state with snapshots: its exact text, buttons with disabled and aria-busy, alert and status regions, the organization select, hero and progress classes. The native publication dialog is its own design; what its states say and offer is asserted by cloud-publish-dialog-states and cloud-publish-organization-choice, and its readiness (repository, commit, branch) is prepared rather than reported.

TS's publish task has a completed view and decides what takes precedence over it (a local folder, resolving, loading, an error). The native publication has no completed page: a finished publication is announced in the Header and the folder stays the open project; the dialog's own precedence (a run in flight, then a saved operation, then the first page) is covered by cloud-publish-dialog-states.
